name: Chicken, mushroom, broccoli & spinach glass-noodle stir-fry (logged batch)

source.author: User's logged batch — cooked 2026-08-22
source.notes: Reference log of a batch the user actually cooked (exact amounts below; 100 g spinach added after the initial log). No oil or sauce was specified — assumed ~1 tbsp oil for stir-frying and light salt/pepper seasoning; sodium is low as-computed and rises if soy/salt is added. Tell me the oil/soy used and I'll adjust. Mushrooms ~150 g (8), onion ~75 g (½), zucchini ~400 g (2).

steps: Sear chicken strips, then stir-fry the veg and noodles together, folding spinach in at the end.

batch_totals.note: Sodium low as-computed (~640 mg batch) — rises with any added soy/salt.

him.verdict: A lean, high-protein cutting plate — 40 g protein for ~414 kcal (~9.8 g protein per 100 kcal) and only ~8 g fat/serving, with a big volume of veg and ~4 g fiber. The spinach + broccoli bring folate, vitamin C and iron; mushrooms add selenium (a sperm micro). Low sodium AS COOKED here (no heavy sauce) — a plus versus the soy-loaded stir-fries. Glass noodles are the one refined carb, well balanced by the protein and veg.
flags: 40 g protein/serving, very lean (~8 g fat)
suggested_mods: If you season with soy, use low-sodium and go light — that's the only thing that would push sodium up
Finish with a squeeze of lemon/lime to lift it

her_preconception.verdict: Strong for her — the 100 g spinach plus broccoli make this a real FOLATE dish (~65 mcg DFE/serving, the top preconception nutrient), with iron (~2.7 mg) paired with the veg's vitamin C for absorption, plus choline and selenium on lean protein. Fully cooked, no sprouts, no high-mercury fish — no safety flags. Low sodium as cooked. One of the better everyday preconception mains.
prenatal_highlights: folate from spinach + broccoli (~65 mcg DFE/serving) — top preconception nutrient
iron (~2.7 mg) paired with vitamin C (broccoli/spinach) for absorption
choline + selenium; lean protein; low sodium as cooked
suggested_mods: Keep it lightly seasoned to hold the sodium down
Already folate-strong; a lemon squeeze adds a little more vitamin C

cooking_guide: Prep everything first — stir-fry moves fast. Soak the glass noodles in warm water until pliable (5-10 min), drain, and snip shorter with scissors.
Steam or blanch the broccoli ~2 min (it's the densest veg), then drain — this way it cooks evenly and stays bright and crisp-tender.
Pat the chicken strips dry and season lightly. Heat the pan/wok hot before the oil goes in — high heat sears, low heat steams.
Stir-fry the chicken in a single layer until just cooked, then remove (crowding makes it grey and watery).
Stir-fry the garlic and onion briefly, then the mushrooms — leave the mushrooms undisturbed a minute to brown (moving them too soon makes them release water and steam).
Add the zucchini and blanched broccoli and toss 2-3 min to keep them crisp-tender.
Return the chicken, add the noodles, and season to taste (salt/pepper, or a splash of low-sodium soy); toss 1-2 min to combine and heat through.
Fold in the spinach at the very end and toss just until wilted — seconds only; overcooking dulls it and loses folate.
Serve promptly. Tip: a squeeze of lemon or lime at the end lifts the whole dish.
